To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the PRRSV N protein is capable of self-association and that disulfide link-ages are involved in the formation and stabilization of the virion.

the porcine N protein forms homodimers that become specifically disulfided linked within the PRRSV-infected cell, the disulfide linkers are formed as a result spurious oxidation during lysis of the virus-infected cells, the disulfided linkers impart stability to the PRRSV virion, and the N-N interactions occur both in the presence as well as absence of disulfide linkage.

(i) PRRSV N protein is a homodimer, (ii) N-N interactions are mediated both by noncovalent and disulfide-linked interactions, and (iii) the disulfide link between the N protein homodimer occurs in the virion and not in infected cells, and it is mediated by cysteine residue 23 of the N protein.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the oligomeric structure of the N protein of the PRRV and the role of intermolecular and intramolecular disulfide bridges in this process.
the assembly and replication mechanisms of PRRSV.
understanding the assembly pathway and the role of the N protein in PRRSV virion formation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

PRRSV nucleoprotein (N) protein is a monomer in the cytoplasm, and it forms homodimers and higher-order structures in the endoplasmatic reticulum (ER) by disulfide bonds and noncovalent interaction, respectively.
N protein homomers (dimers) are the basic building block in the assembly of the PRRSV nucleoprotein complex.
the N protein forms homodimers through both noncovalent and covalent (disulfide bond) interactions, and that the N protein is able to assemble into higher-ordered structures in vitro.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the N protein forms dimers, trimmers, tetramers and pentamers through noncovalent interaction, which may be stabilized by disulfide link.
the N protein of PRRSV is a dimeric protein that can form intermolecular disulphide linkages.
the N protein of PRRSV has the ability to self-associate into homodimers, trimers, and higher-order structures.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the N protein of PRRSV has a propensity to homo-oligomerize and that this is mediated by both noncovalent and covalent interactions.
PRRSV N proteins form disulfide-linked dimers in the virion and that these dimers are stable in the presence of NEM.
the N protein is capable of self-assembly into higher-order oligomeric structures, which are stabilized by disulfide linkers and possibly by RNA.
